verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents several agent-usable write paths: an Admin API covering everything the dashboard does, including creating and updating flags; an official CLI for managing flags; and an official MCP server that lets agents manage flags in IDE sessions or CI/CD. For governance, it documents four-eyes Change Requests (create, approve, publish), RBAC to restrict who can modify production, and Release Pipelines that auto-generate change requests when promoting to production. missing for 10: explicit documentation that change-request enforcement applies to API/CLI/MCP writes made by agent tokens, independent or hands-on corroboration of an agent being blocked pending approval, and a published OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404).

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: Anything you can do in the Flagsmith dashboard, you can also do via the Admin API.
Purpose: Creating, updating, and deleting projects, environments, flags, segments, and users.
The Flagsmith CLI lets you manage flags, segments, features, projects and environments from your terminal
Your assistant can manage feature flags, segments, multivariate options, and release workflows on your behalf — in a human-in-the-loop IDE session, or fully automated in a CI/CD pipeline.
Feature Change Requests help creating a four-eyes workflow (create, approve, publish) to updating feature flags, similarly to Pull Requests in GitHub.
Only allow certain users to modify your production environments.
Release Pipelines can automatically generate change requests when promoting flags to production
